title: Phishing via Signal and Telegram targets European journalists and politicians, Le Monde reports
date_note: Date of the UNN and Slovo i Delo articles relaying Le Monde's investigation; neither gives an earlier day for the report. The campaign is said to have run since at least mid-October.
place: France (Le Monde's reporting; targets across Europe)
geo_basis: country of the reporting outlet and one named target (French MP); targets are in several European countries
summary: Citing Le Monde, UNN and Slovo i Delo report a phishing campaign via Signal and Telegram against European journalists, politicians and activists, running since at least mid-October. Messages appear to come from acquaintances and link to fake pages seeking logins and codes. Le Monde's European sources link it to UNC5792; Google's John Hultquist is cited as saying the methods match that group.
plain: Fake messages from supposed acquaintances on Signal and Telegram are reportedly being used to steal logins from European journalists and politicians. The reports rely on Le Monde and its sources.
exec: Messaging-app phishing aimed at journalists and politicians is reported; the attribution comes from Le Monde's sources and has not been read at the original.
action: General advice: treat unexpected invitations to video calls or Telegram groups, even from known contacts, as suspect, and confirm them through another channel before clicking.
impact: Named targets in the reports include Christo Grozev, Bastian Obermayer, three Le Monde employees and French MP Eric Bothorel.

validation.note: UNN and Slovo i Delo both relay one Le Monde investigation, so this is a single source; Le Monde's original was not read. Attribution to UNC5792 and an FSB unit is by Le Monde's sources and (per the articles) US authorities, not confirmed by a page read here.

review.note: Compared title, date, mid-October start, targets, method and UNC5792 attribution (Le Monde sources; Hultquist in Slovo i Delo) with UNN and Slovo i Delo; developing and single_source fit
